title: Sum of Two Numbers
statement:
Given two integers a and b, print their sum.

Input: one line with two integers a and b (|a|, |b| <= 10^9).
Output: a single integer, the value of a + b.

title: Palindrome Check
statement:
A string is a palindrome if it reads the same forwards and backwards. Given a string of lowercase letters, decide whether it is a palindrome.

Input: one line containing the string s (1 <= |s| <= 1000).
Output: YES if s is a palindrome, otherwise NO.

title: Count Vowels
statement:
Count how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u) appear in a line of text made of lowercase letters and spaces.

Input: one line of text (at most 1000 characters).
Output: a single integer, the number of vowels.

title: Maximum Element
statement:
Given an array of integers, find its largest element.

Input: the first line contains n (1 <= n <= 1000). The second line contains n integers.
Output: the maximum value in the array.

title: Sort Descending
statement:
Sort an array of integers from largest to smallest.

Input: the first line contains n (1 <= n <= 1000). The second line contains n integers.
Output: the n integers in non-increasing order, separated by single spaces.

title: Prime Check
statement:
A prime number is greater than 1 and has no divisors other than 1 and itself. Decide whether a given number is prime.

Input: one integer n (1 <= n <= 10^9).
Output: YES if n is prime, otherwise NO.

title: Factorial Modulo
statement:
Compute n! (n factorial, the product 1 * 2 * ... * n, with 0! = 1) modulo 1000000007.

Input: one integer n (0 <= n <= 1000).
Output: n! mod 1000000007.

title: Balanced Brackets
statement:
A string made only of the characters ( ) [ ] { } is balanced if every opening bracket is closed by the same kind of bracket in the correct order. Decide whether the given string is balanced.

Input: one line with the string (1 <= length <= 1000).
Output: YES if the string is balanced, otherwise NO.

title: Fibonacci Number
statement:
The Fibonacci sequence starts with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1, and each next term is the sum of the previous two. Compute F(n) modulo 1000000007 using dynamic programming.

Input: one integer n (0 <= n <= 100000).
Output: F(n) mod 1000000007.

title: Connected Components
statement:
An undirected graph has n vertices numbered 1 to n and m edges. Count its connected components, where a component is a maximal set of vertices that can reach each other through edges.

Input: the first line contains n and m. Each of the next m lines contains two vertices u and v joined by an edge.
Output: the number of connected components.

title: Shortest Path in a Grid
statement:
A grid has n rows and m columns. Each cell is free ('.') or a wall ('#'). Starting at the top-left cell you may move one step up, down, left or right onto a free cell. Find the minimum number of steps needed to reach the bottom-right cell, or report that it is impossible.

Input: the first line contains n and m. Each of the next n lines contains m characters.
Output: the minimum number of steps, or -1 if the bottom-right cell cannot be reached.

title: Minimum Coins
statement:
You have an unlimited supply of coins of given denominations. Find the minimum number of coins needed to make an exact amount, or report that it is impossible. This is a classic dynamic programming problem.

Input: the first line contains n (number of denominations) and the target amount (0 <= amount <= 10000). The second line contains the n coin values.
Output: the minimum number of coins, or -1 if the amount cannot be made.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement:
Given an array of integers, find the length of its longest strictly increasing subsequence. A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip elements. Solve it with dynamic programming.

Input: the first line contains n (1 <= n <= 1000). The second line contains n integers.
Output: the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
